episodes.title: Breakfast Wrap: Has AI ended maths as we know it?

stories.angle: Have mathematicians lost the race to artificial intelligence?
stories.voices: Luke Siddall-Dunstan, Presenter; Stephen Strogatz, US mathematician and author (pre-recorded, unchallenged)
stories.tone: Explanatory, intrigued, and slightly alarmed about the rapid pace of change.
stories.emphasis: Theoretical implications, complexity of mathematical problems, and the role of AI models like the Riemann hypothesis.
stories.placement: Lead item, major focus of the episode.
stories.evidence: "Calculators were not philosophically threatening. This is a whole different universe now."

stories.angle: Government efforts to secure support for digital duty of care laws and foreign interference concerns.
stories.voices: Luke Siddall-Dunstan, Presenter; Penny Wong, Foreign Minister (clip); Sue Keay, co-author of the report, Director of the UNSW AI Institute (pre-recorded, unchallenged)
stories.emphasis: National security, tech giants, foreign interference, and digital safety.
stories.evidence: "Artificial intelligence is reshaping the foundations of our societies, cyber attacks are more frequent…"

stories.story: Digital Duty of Care and Social Media Laws
stories.angle: The federal government securing support for laws targeting big tech companies over harm caused online.
stories.voices: Luke Siddall-Dunstan, Presenter; Anika Wells, Minister for Communications and Minister for Sport (pre-recorded, challenged in tone of questioning); David Bradt, US Ambassador to Australia (clip)
stories.emphasis: Accountability of tech platforms, penalties, free speech, and the effectiveness of regulation.
stories.evidence: "The government has secured support for a number of changes to its proposed digital duty of care."

episodes.title: Deakin University | How AI is helping screen cerebral palsy

stories.angle: How artificial intelligence is being used to help screen cerebral palsy in infants.
stories.voices: Sasha Barba-Gat, Presenter; Romero Moreys, Deakin University Research Fellow (pre-recorded, unchallenged)
stories.emphasis: Early detection, infant healthcare, accessibility of medical diagnosis, and technological innovation.
stories.evidence: "That's happening through Deakin University's applied artificial intelligence initiative."

stories.angle: Why so many different countries are stuck in the same economic funk.
stories.voices: Sasha Barba-Gat, Presenter; Various anonymous commentators and international experts (clips)
stories.emphasis: Global economic indicators, cost of living, political fatigue, and international comparisons.
stories.evidence: "We're asking why so many different countries are stuck in the same funk."

episodes.title: How many job losses does the RBA want?

stories.angle: The Reserve Bank of Australia maintaining high interest rates and the impact on unemployment.
stories.voices: Sam Hawley, Presenter; Jim Chalmers, Treasurer (clip); Michele Bullock, Reserve Bank Governor (clip); Jessica Irvine, Money Correspondent (live interview, unchallenged); Sally Sara, journalist (clip)
stories.tone: Critical, serious, and questioning of economic policy.
stories.emphasis: Employment figures, cost of living, monetary policy, and the trade-off between inflation and jobs.
stories.placement: Lead item, sole focus of the episode.
stories.evidence: "The Reserve Bank has raised the cash rate to 4.85%, a level not seen in Australia since 2008."
